memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD is my strength and my defense; he has become my salvation. He is my
God, and I will praise him, my father's God, and I will exalt him."
- Ex 15:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at how personal this becomes. My strength. My defence. My salvation. My
God.

The whole nation is singing, but each voice is saying "my." That is an important
balance. Faith is never merely private, yet it must be personal. You can stand
in a crowd of believers and still need to say "my God" for yourself.

Then comes a beautiful phrase: "my father's God." Here are two things held
together. The God I have come to know personally is also the God my father
knew. Israel had inherited a faith, and now they had experienced it themselves.

Many of us were given faith by parents or grandparents. That inheritance is a
gift, not a weakness. But it must become ours. Timothy had a faith that "first
lived in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice and, I am persuaded,
now lives in you also" (2 Tim 1:5). Notice Paul's careful wording. It lived in
them; now it lives in him.

If you are living on someone else's faith, this song invites you further in. And
if you came to Christ with no Christian family at all, you have now begun a "my
father's God" for someone who comes after you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you say "my God," or only "our family's God"?
2. Who might one day speak of your faith as an inheritance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are my strength and my salvation, not just my family's. Make my faith
truly my own, and let it bless those who come after me. Amen.
